verses.text: Listen, heavens, and I'll speak. Let the earth hear what I have to say.
Let my teaching fall like rain and my words settle like dew, like a mist over tender grass and showers over green plants.
I'll proclaim the LORD's name. Give our God the praise his greatness deserves!
He is the Rock. Everything he does is perfect, and all his ways are fair. He's faithful and does no wrong. He's just and upright.
They acted dishonestly toward him. Their own corruption shows they're no longer his children. They're a twisted and crooked generation.
Is this how you repay the LORD, you foolish people with no sense? Isn't he your Father, the one who bought you, made you, and established you?
Remember the old days. Think back through the generations. Ask your father, and he'll explain. Ask your elders, and they'll tell you.
When the Most High handed out land to the nations and separated the human race, he set the peoples' boundaries according to the number of the Israelites.
The LORD's share is his people. Jacob is the inheritance that belongs to him.
He found Jacob in a desert, in a barren wilderness where the wind howled. He surrounded him, cared for him, and guarded him like the pupil of his own eye.
Like an eagle stirring up her nest and hovering over her young, the LORD spread his wings, caught them, and carried them on his feathers.
The LORD alone led Jacob. No foreign god was with him.
He let him ride over the heights of the earth and eat what the fields produced. He gave him honey from rock and oil from flint,
butter from his cattle and milk from his flock, fat from lambs, the rams of Bashan and goats, and the finest wheat. You drank wine, the blood of the grape.
But Jeshurun grew fat and kicked. You grew fat, thick, and sleek. Then he abandoned the God who made him and rejected the Rock who saved him.
They stirred up his jealousy with foreign gods and made him angry with detestable things.
They sacrificed to demons instead of God, to gods they'd never known, new gods that had just shown up and that their ancestors had never feared.
You stopped thinking about the Rock who fathered you. You forgot the God who gave you birth.
The LORD saw what his sons and daughters were doing to provoke him and recoiled in disgust.
He said, “I'll hide my face from them and see how they end up. They're a twisted generation, children with no faithfulness.
They made me jealous with something that isn't God and provoked me with worthless idols. I'll make them jealous with people who don't even count as a nation. I'll provoke them with a foolish nation.
My anger has started a fire that burns down to the depths of Sheol. It consumes the earth and what it produces and sets the roots of the mountains on fire.
I'll pile disasters on them and use up my arrows against them.
Hunger will waste them away. Burning heat and bitter destruction will consume them. I'll send beasts to bite them and the venom of vipers that slide through the dust.
Outside, the sword will take their loved ones. Inside their rooms, terror will strike young men and young women, nursing babies and gray-haired men alike.
I said I'd scatter them far away and wipe out their memory from among humanity.
But I held back for fear the enemy would take it the wrong way and boast, ‘Our hand is mighty. The LORD had nothing to do with this.’”
They're a nation with no good judgment. There's no understanding in them.
If only they were wise enough to understand this and think about how it will end for them!
How could one person chase a thousand or two put ten thousand to flight unless their Rock had sold them and the LORD had handed them over?
Their rock can't compare to our Rock. Even our enemies admit it.
Their vine comes from Sodom's vine and Gomorrah's fields. Their grapes are poisonous and their clusters bitter.
Their wine is snake poison, the cruel venom of deadly snakes.
“Isn't all this stored away with me, sealed up among my treasures?
Vengeance and repayment are mine. Their time will come when their feet slip. Their day of disaster is close, and their ruin is rushing toward them.”
The LORD will judge his people and have compassion on his servants when he sees their strength is gone and no one remains, confined or free.
He'll ask, “Where are their gods now? Where's the rock they ran to for shelter?
Where are the gods that ate the fat of their sacrifices and drank the wine of their offerings? Let those gods get up and help you. Let them protect you!
See now that I myself am God. There's no god beside me. I take life and give life. I wound and I heal. Nobody can rescue anyone from my hand.
I raise my hand toward heaven and declare that, as surely as I live forever,
when I sharpen my gleaming sword and take hold of judgment, I'll take vengeance on my enemies and repay those who hate me.
I'll make my arrows drunk with blood. My sword will devour flesh, with the blood of the dead and the captives and with the heads of the enemy leaders.”
Rejoice with his people, you nations! He'll avenge the blood of his servants, repay his enemies, and make atonement for his land and his people.
Moses and Joshua son of Nun came and recited all the words of this song for the people to hear.
When Moses finished saying all these words to Israel,
he told them, “Take to heart every word I'm giving you as a witness today. Tell your children to carefully follow every word of this law.
These words matter. They are your life. By living by them, you'll have long lives in the land you're crossing the Jordan to take as your own.”
That same day the LORD spoke to Moses.
“Go up to Mount Nebo in the Abarim range, in Moab across from Jericho. Look out over Canaan, the land I'm giving the Israelites to possess.
You'll die on the mountain you climb and be gathered to your people, just as your brother Aaron died on Mount Hor and was gathered to his people.
This is because you broke faith with me in front of the Israelites at the waters of Meribah at Kadesh, in the wilderness of Zin. You failed to honor my holiness among the Israelites.
You'll see the land from far away, but you won't enter the land I'm giving to the Israelites.”
